rationale: C08 is the closest because both letters concern economic reporting under the Employment Act of 1946 and identify the Council of Economic Advisers, but the earlier letter merely transmits a statutory report and does not share the child's signing-announcement structure, subscription/publication mechanism, or appreciatory close. C12 shares the routine request to convey presidential appreciation to members of an organization, while C02 emphasizes communicating economic facts to Congress and the public. These overlaps are generic or arise from the same policy and institutional setting, not from a concrete, material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Employment Act of 1946 ... economic charts and statistics prepared for the Joint Committee on the Economic Report by the Council of Economic Advisers
shared_material.parent_excerpt: transmitted in accordance with section 3 (b) of the Employment Act of 1946 ... prepared for me by the Council of Economic Advisers
shared_material.explanation: C08 shares the statute, subject matter, and advisory body, but uses them for a different statutory-report transmission and lacks the child's distinctive operative content.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Please convey to each member of the Joint Committee ... my appreciation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Please convey to the Commander ... and to all of the member[s] ... my commendation
shared_material.explanation: C12 has a similar convey-my-appreciation formulation, but this is routine correspondence language and is not material enough to establish templating.

shared_material.child_excerpt: bringing basic economic facts to the attention of the Congress and the people
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The facts speak for themselves. The people know ...
shared_material.explanation: C02 likewise stresses informing Congress and the public through economic facts, but the wording and structure are not sufficiently distinctive or parallel.
